rules: Ordinary applied-playbook authoring defaults to FAST_EDIT without asking the user to choose a verification mode.
After a local edit, run only the minimum mechanically justified checks for the changed scope and its direct dependency closure.
A verified checkpoint is trusted as the regression baseline; subsequent authoring verifies the delta from that checkpoint instead of replaying previously proven history.
PLAYBOOK_VERIFY is required before an applied playbook is handed off, shared as a working candidate, or promoted to a verified checkpoint.
FULL_VERIFY/FULL_FACTORY is reserved for explicit milestone/finalization/readiness/acceptance, shared factory or canonical foundation changes, or unknown/ambiguous impact.
A text-only edit must not trigger full playbook or factory regression unless impact analysis proves that the edited text is itself shared executable policy.
FAST_EDIT and PLAYBOOK_VERIFY are feedback/readiness scopes and must never be reported as full release verification.
Measure verification wall-clock time. Material slowdown of a previously fast contour is a DX regression to investigate rather than silently accepting broader checks.
PLAYBOOK_VERIFY for a generated candidate must include the Vibe-owned generated_playbook_contract and replay-package validation before analyst-visible handoff.
Known machine-detectable generated-playbook defects are repaired inside the Vibe loop; do not spend analyst time on YAML/editor-contract debugging that trusted gates can detect.
Target first analyst-visible alpha within about 10 minutes when source inputs are sufficient; investigate loops dominated by repeated Editor/YAML repair as a factory regression.

interaction_contract.normal_loop: user request -> apply change -> minimal affected checks -> concise result -> continue
full_verification_trigger: user explicitly asks to finalize/release/fully verify
impact closure is unknown or ambiguous
interaction_contract.checkpoint_use: Promote coherent passing states frequently so future checks use checkpoint delta rather than full history.

time_expectations.FAST_EDIT: seconds for a small applied playbook; investigate strong regression
time_expectations.PLAYBOOK_VERIFY: tens of seconds to local-playbook minutes depending on fixtures; no factory-wide suite
time_expectations.FULL_FACTORY: may be slow and is intentionally rare
